Source of truth: data/Results_130226_SSM.xlsx, sheet "APEC_driftsformsjekk_120226 (2)".
This is the per-isolate table (1 row = 1 isolate) where driftsformnavn has already
been backfilled from the external "driftsform_sjekket" lookup (see 1_data_wrangling.qmd) -
the earlier "APEC_all_enterobase_cleaned_260" sheet still has driftsformnavn = NA for
562/884 isolates and should NOT be used for the broiler/parent split.
The other pre-aggregated summary sheets in the workbook are not used here; every
figure below aggregates from this single per-isolate table so all counts stay

# Setup
```{r setup}
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(scales)
library(ggalluvial)
```

```{r source reused functions}
fun_files_path <- c(
  list.files(here::here(params$source_code), pattern = "*.R$", full.names = TRUE),
  list.files(here::here(params$source_viz), pattern = "*.R$", full.names = TRUE)
)
sapply(fun_files_path, source, .GlobalEnv)
```

# Data import

```{r load data}
isolates_raw <- read_excel(
  here::here(params$results_xlsx),
  sheet = params$isolate_sheet
)
```

# Data quality checks

One row must equal one isolate, and the key fields used across every figure
below (year, ST, serotype, production type) must be complete - if any of these
checks fail, stop and fix the import rather than silently plotting partial data.

```{r qc checks}
qc <- list(
  n_rows = nrow(isolates_raw),
  n_distinct_sample = n_distinct(isolates_raw$Sample),
  n_missing_year = sum(is.na(isolates_raw$Year)),
  n_missing_ST = sum(is.na(isolates_raw[["mlst_scheme_list/sequence_type"]])),
  n_missing_serotype = sum(is.na(isolates_raw[["SeroTypeFinder/SeroType"]])),
  n_missing_driftsform = sum(is.na(isolates_raw$driftsformnavn)),
  driftsform_categories = unique(isolates_raw$driftsformnavn)
)
qc

stopifnot(
  "one row per isolate expected" = qc$n_rows == qc$n_distinct_sample,
  "Year must be complete" = qc$n_missing_year == 0,
  "ST must be complete" = qc$n_missing_ST == 0,
  "Serotype must be complete" = qc$n_missing_serotype == 0,
  "driftsformnavn must be complete" = qc$n_missing_driftsform == 0
)
```

# Cleaning: production type (broiler / parent flock)

`driftsformnavn` has a known mojibake artifact (2 rows read as
"Foreldredyr, kj�ttproduksjon" instead of "Foreldredyr, kjøttproduksjon" - same
category, corrupted ø). Matching on the "Foreldredyr" prefix sidesteps the
encoding issue entirely and translates straight to the English labels used in
all figures.

```{r clean driftsform}
isolates <- isolates_raw %>%
  mutate(
    production_type = case_when(
      str_starts(driftsformnavn, "Foreldredyr") ~ "Parent flock",
      driftsformnavn == "Kjøttproduksjon" ~ "Broiler",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    production_type = factor(production_type, levels = c("Broiler", "Parent flock")),
    ST = as.character(.data[["mlst_scheme_list/sequence_type"]]),
    Serotype = .data[["SeroTypeFinder/SeroType"]],
    Year = as.integer(Year)
  )

stopifnot("production_type must be complete after recoding" = sum(is.na(isolates$production_type)) == 0)

count(isolates, production_type)
```

# Cleaning: virulence genes (long format)

Same parsing logic as `1_data_wrangling.qmd`: split the semicolon-free,
comma-separated "Gene: Description" string into one row per isolate per gene,
then de-duplicate (a gene can be listed more than once per isolate, e.g.
multiple copies detected).

```{r virulence genes long}
core_genes <- c("hlyF", "iroN", "iss", "iucC", "iutA", "ompT")

virulence_long <- isolates %>%
  select(Sample, Year, production_type, ST, Serotype, tosplit = `Virulence_Finder/VirulenceGenes:ProteinName`) %>%
  separate_longer_delim(tosplit, delim = ",") %>%
  separate(tosplit, into = c("VF_gene_name", "VF_gene_description"), sep = ": ", fill = "right") %>%
  mutate(across(c(VF_gene_name, VF_gene_description), str_trim)) %>%
  distinct()

# genes present in >= 1 isolate but excluded from the "variable virulence" figures
# because they are core to ~all APEC isolates in this dataset
virulence_long_variable <- virulence_long %>%
  filter(!VF_gene_name %in% core_genes)

n_distinct(virulence_long$VF_gene_name)
n_distinct(virulence_long_variable$VF_gene_name)
```

# ST x Serotype combination table

Clean counts of every observed ST x Serotype combination, isolate counts only
(per Solveig/collaborator instruction - not per-animal). Exported in full so it
can be reviewed and the >=10 threshold adjusted later without re-running R.

```{r st serotype table}
st_serotype_counts <- isolates %>%
  count(ST, Serotype, name = "n_isolates") %>%
  arrange(desc(n_isolates))

dir.create(here::here("results", "tables"), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
write_csv(st_serotype_counts, here::here("results", "tables", "ST_serotype_combination_counts.csv"))

st_serotype_counts %>% filter(n_isolates >= 10) %>% nrow()  # combinations shown in the main figure
st_serotype_counts %>% filter(n_isolates < 10) %>% nrow()   # combinations pushed to appendix
```

# Draft visualisations

Each section below is a candidate chart for discussion with collaborators.
Save drafts with `save_apec_plot(p, "name.png", stage = "drafts")`
(writes to `results/figures/drafts/`, gitignored).

## Figure 1: Sampling timeline (isolates + insendelser per year, by production type)

Covers must-haves #1 (year distribution / bias check), #2 (insendelser vs.
isolates per year), #4 (broiler/parent distinction) and #5 (isolate-level
counts) in one figure. Two panels avoid a dual y-axis: isolate counts and
insendelse (sak) counts are not on the same scale, so they get separate panels
with independent y-axes (`scales = "free_y"`) rather than being forced onto one.

```{r figure1 data}
timeline_data <- bind_rows(
  isolates %>%
    count(Year, production_type, name = "n") %>%
    mutate(metric = "Isolates"),
  isolates %>%
    distinct(Year, sak, production_type) %>%
    count(Year, production_type, name = "n") %>%
    mutate(metric = "Insendelser (sak)")
) %>%
  mutate(metric = factor(metric, levels = c("Isolates", "Insendelser (sak)")))
```

**Proposal A - stacked bars, faceted by metric:**

```{r figure1a}
fig1a <- timeline_data %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Year, y = n, fill = production_type)) +
  geom_col(color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  facet_wrap(~metric, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2018:2025) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = palette_qual[1:2]) +
  labs(
    title = "APEC sampling, 2018–2025",
    subtitle = "Isolate and submission (insendelse) counts per year, by production type",
    x = NULL, y = "Count", fill = "Production type"
  ) +
  theme_apec()

fig1a
save_apec_plot(fig1a, "fig1a_timeline_stacked.png", stage = "drafts")
```

**Proposal B - dodged bars, same panels:**
Dodged bars make it easier to compare broiler vs. parent flock magnitude
directly within a year (stacking makes reading the *smaller* segment's exact
height harder); the tradeoff is a slightly busier plot.

```{r figure1b}
fig1b <- timeline_data %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Year, y = n, fill = production_type)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge2(preserve = "single"), color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  facet_wrap(~metric, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2018:2025) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = palette_qual[1:2]) +
  labs(
    title = "APEC sampling, 2018–2025",
    subtitle = "Isolate and submission (insendelse) counts per year, by production type",
    x = NULL, y = "Count", fill = "Production type"
  ) +
  theme_apec()

fig1b
save_apec_plot(fig1b, "fig1b_timeline_dodged.png", stage = "drafts")
```

## Figure 2: ST x Serotype combinations (>=10 isolates), by production type

Only the 17 combinations with >= 10 isolates are shown directly (the full
117-combination tail is in `results/tables/ST_serotype_combination_counts.csv`
for appendix use). Horizontal bars keep the "ST : Serotype" labels readable
without rotated text; ordering by total count turns the ranking into the
visual read.

```{r figure2}
combo_threshold <- 10

top_combos <- isolates %>%
  mutate(combo = paste(ST, Serotype, sep = " : ")) %>%
  count(combo, name = "n_total") %>%
  filter(n_total >= combo_threshold)

fig2_data <- isolates %>%
  mutate(combo = paste(ST, Serotype, sep = " : ")) %>%
  filter(combo %in% top_combos$combo) %>%
  count(combo, production_type, name = "n") %>%
  left_join(top_combos, by = "combo") %>%
  mutate(combo = fct_reorder(combo, n_total))

fig2 <- fig2_data %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = n, y = combo, fill = production_type)) +
  geom_col(color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = palette_qual[1:2]) +
  labs(
    title = "Most common ST × Serotype combinations",
    subtitle = paste0("Combinations with ≥", combo_threshold, " isolates (", nrow(top_combos), " of ", nrow(st_serotype_counts), " total combinations shown)"),
    x = "Number of isolates", y = NULL, fill = "Production type"
  ) +
  theme_apec() +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())

fig2
save_apec_plot(fig2, "fig2_st_serotype_top.png", stage = "drafts")
```

## Figure 3: ST x Serotype combinations by year (heatmap)

Addresses the "per-year distribution of the top ST x Serotype combinations,
split by production type" ask. A heatmap is the right form here: two
categorical axes (combo x year) with a magnitude (count) is exactly a
"compare magnitude on a grid" job, and it scales far better than 17 x 8 x 2
grouped bars would. Sequential single-hue fill (not categorical) because the
job is magnitude, not identity. Cells are faceted by production type rather
than color-coded by it, since color is already spent on count.

```{r figure3}
fig3_data <- isolates %>%
  mutate(combo = paste(ST, Serotype, sep = " : ")) %>%
  filter(combo %in% top_combos$combo) %>%
  count(combo, Year, production_type, name = "n") %>%
  complete(combo, Year, production_type, fill = list(n = 0)) %>%
  left_join(top_combos, by = "combo") %>%
  mutate(combo = fct_reorder(combo, n_total))

fig3 <- fig3_data %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(Year), y = combo, fill = n)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(n == 0, "", n)), size = 2.8, color = "grey20") +
  facet_wrap(~production_type) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#f7f7f7", high = palette_qual[1], na.value = "white") +
  labs(
    title = "ST × Serotype combinations by year and production type",
    subtitle = paste0("Combinations with ≥", combo_threshold, " isolates total; cell = isolate count"),
    x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "Isolates"
  ) +
  theme_apec() +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "right")

fig3
save_apec_plot(fig3, "fig3_st_serotype_by_year.png", stage = "drafts", width = 26, height = 16)
```

## Figure 3b: ST x Serotype flow, by production type (alluvial - alternative to the heatmap)

Same underlying question as Figure 3 (how do production type, ST and Serotype
relate for the common combinations), shown as flow instead of a grid. Each
ribbon is a group of isolates; ribbon width = isolate count. This is a
genuinely different read from the heatmap: it emphasizes *how much of each ST*
routes to *which serotype* and *which production type*, at the cost of not
showing year and getting cluttered past ~10-15 categories per axis - which is
exactly why it's restricted to the same >=10-isolate combos as Figures 2-3.
`ggalluvial` is a new dependency for this project (added to renv.lock).

```{r figure3b alluvial data}
alluvial_data <- isolates %>%
  mutate(combo = paste(ST, Serotype, sep = " : ")) %>%
  filter(combo %in% top_combos$combo) %>%
  count(production_type, ST, Serotype, name = "n") %>%
  # keep ST/Serotype ordered by overall frequency so the biggest flows sit together
  left_join(isolates %>% count(ST, name = "n_ST"), by = "ST") %>%
  left_join(isolates %>% count(Serotype, name = "n_Serotype"), by = "Serotype") %>%
  mutate(
    ST = fct_reorder(ST, n_ST, .desc = TRUE),
    Serotype = fct_reorder(Serotype, n_Serotype, .desc = TRUE)
  )
```

```{r figure3b}
fig3b <- alluvial_data %>%
  ggplot(aes(axis1 = production_type, axis2 = ST, axis3 = Serotype, y = n)) +
  geom_alluvium(aes(fill = production_type), width = 1/4, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_stratum(width = 1/4, fill = "grey95", color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_text(stat = "stratum", aes(label = after_stat(stratum)), size = 2.8) +
  scale_x_discrete(limits = c("Production type", "ST", "Serotype"), expand = c(0.08, 0.08)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = palette_qual[1:2]) +
  labs(
    title = "ST × Serotype flow, by production type",
    subtitle = paste0("Combinations with ≥", combo_threshold, " isolates total (year not shown - see Figure 3 heatmap for the yearly breakdown)"),
    x = NULL, y = "Isolates", fill = "Production type"
  ) +
  theme_apec() +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )

fig3b
save_apec_plot(fig3b, "fig3b_st_serotype_alluvial.png", stage = "drafts", width = 24, height = 20)
```

## Figure 3c: ST x Serotype flow, faceted by year, with crossing-reduced axis order

**Rejected (2026-07-30): labels too small to read, not usable for
publication.** Kept for the record and in case the underlying small-multiples
idea is worth revisiting at a larger size later; superseded for now by Figure
3d (one year per page, same data, readable) for exploration/supplement use.

Two changes from Figure 3b, both purely about *plotting order* - no data is
added, removed, or recalculated:

1. **Faceted by year** to bring back the temporal dimension the alluvial in
   3b dropped.
2. **Barycenter-ordered axes.** By default the ST and Serotype axes are
   ordered by raw frequency, which is what made 3b's ST -> Serotype junction
   tangled (a frequency-ordered ST next to a frequency-ordered Serotype has no
   reason to line up). Instead, each ST is positioned by the weighted-average
   position of the production types it flows from, and each Serotype is
   positioned by the weighted-average position of the STs it flows from (the
   standard barycenter/median heuristic used to reduce crossings in
   Sankey-style diagrams). Same 17 combinations, same counts - only the left-
   to-right order of the categories on the ST and Serotype axes changes.

```{r figure3c ordering}
production_order <- c("Broiler" = 1, "Parent flock" = 2)

st_order <- alluvial_data %>%
  mutate(prod_pos = production_order[as.character(production_type)]) %>%
  group_by(ST) %>%
  summarise(bary = weighted.mean(prod_pos, w = n), n_total = sum(n), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(bary, desc(n_total)) %>%
  pull(ST) %>%
  as.character()

serotype_order <- alluvial_data %>%
  mutate(st_pos = match(as.character(ST), st_order)) %>%
  group_by(Serotype) %>%
  summarise(bary = weighted.mean(st_pos, w = n), n_total = sum(n), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(bary, desc(n_total)) %>%
  pull(Serotype) %>%
  as.character()

alluvial_data_ordered <- alluvial_data %>%
  mutate(
    ST = factor(as.character(ST), levels = st_order),
    Serotype = factor(as.character(Serotype), levels = serotype_order)
  )
```

```{r figure3c data}
fig3c_data <- isolates %>%
  mutate(combo = paste(ST, Serotype, sep = " : ")) %>%
  filter(combo %in% top_combos$combo) %>%
  count(Year, production_type, ST, Serotype, name = "n") %>%
  mutate(
    ST = factor(ST, levels = st_order),
    Serotype = factor(Serotype, levels = serotype_order)
  )
```

```{r figure3c}
fig3c <- fig3c_data %>%
  ggplot(aes(axis1 = production_type, axis2 = ST, axis3 = Serotype, y = n)) +
  geom_alluvium(aes(fill = production_type), width = 1/4, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_stratum(width = 1/4, fill = "grey95", color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_x_discrete(limits = c("Production type", "ST", "Serotype"), expand = c(0.1, 0.1)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = palette_qual[1:2]) +
  facet_wrap(~Year, ncol = 4) +
  labs(
    title = "ST × Serotype flow, by production type and year",
    subtitle = paste0("Combinations with ≥", combo_threshold, " isolates total; axes ordered to reduce ribbon crossing (see Figure 3b for labeled strata)"),
    x = NULL, y = "Isolates", fill = "Production type"
  ) +
  theme_apec() +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 6),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )

fig3c
save_apec_plot(fig3c, "fig3c_st_serotype_alluvial_by_year.png", stage = "drafts", width = 30, height = 22)
```

```{r figure3e}
fig3e
```

## Figure 3d: ST x Serotype flow, one year per page

Figure 3c's small multiples get cramped for the low-count years. This
produces the same per-year alluvial, but one year per page, at full size, via
`ggforce::facet_wrap_paginate()` - the tool for exactly this ("print facets on
separate pages"). Output is a single multi-page PDF (open it and page through)
plus one PNG per year for quick browsing without a PDF viewer. Free y-scale
per page, since each page stands alone and readability of that single year
matters more than cross-year magnitude comparison (Figure 3c/Figure 1 already
cover the magnitude comparison).

`ggforce` is a new dependency for this project (added to renv.lock).

```{r figure3d setup}
library(ggforce)

fig3d_base <- fig3c_data %>%
  ggplot(aes(axis1 = production_type, axis2 = ST, axis3 = Serotype, y = n)) +
  geom_alluvium(aes(fill = production_type), width = 1/4, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_stratum(width = 1/4, fill = "grey95", color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_text(stat = "stratum", aes(label = after_stat(stratum)), size = 2.3) +
  scale_x_discrete(limits = c("Production type", "ST", "Serotype"), expand = c(0.08, 0.08)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = palette_qual[1:2]) +
  labs(
    title = "ST × Serotype flow, by production type",
    subtitle = paste0("Combinations with ≥", combo_threshold, " isolates total"),
    x = NULL, y = "Isolates", fill = "Production type"
  ) +
  theme_apec() +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom")

n_pg <- n_pages(fig3d_base + facet_wrap_paginate(~Year, ncol = 1, nrow = 1, scales = "free_y", page = 1))
```

```{r figure3d pdf}
pdf_path <- here::here("results", "figures", "drafts", "fig3d_st_serotype_alluvial_by_year_pages.pdf")
pdf(pdf_path, width = 11, height = 13, onefile = TRUE)
for (p in seq_len(n_pg)) {
  print(fig3d_base + facet_wrap_paginate(~Year, ncol = 1, nrow = 1, scales = "free_y", page = p))
}
invisible(dev.off())
```

```{r figure3d pngs}
by_year_dir <- here::here("results", "figures", "drafts", "fig3d_by_year")
dir.create(by_year_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

for (yr in sort(unique(fig3c_data$Year))) {
  p <- fig3d_base + filter(fig3c_data, Year == yr) +
    labs(subtitle = paste0("Year ", yr, " - combinations with ≥", combo_threshold, " isolates total"))
  ggsave(
    filename = file.path(by_year_dir, paste0("fig3d_", yr, ".png")),
    plot = p, width = 24, height = 30, units = "cm", dpi = 300
  )
}
```

## Figure 4: Serotype composition by production type (proportion, not raw count)

Broiler (650 isolates) and Parent flock (234 isolates) group sizes differ a
lot, so raw counts would make Broiler look more "diverse" by default. Showing
% within each production type controls for that and answers the actual
question: do the *proportions* of serotypes differ by production type. Capped
to the serotypes reaching >=2% in at least one group; the rest are folded into
"Other" rather than cycling more hues (there are 115 serotypes total - direct
per-serotype color would break down long before that).

```{r figure4}
serotype_totals <- isolates %>% count(production_type, name = "n_group")

serotype_share <- isolates %>%
  count(production_type, Serotype, name = "n") %>%
  left_join(serotype_totals, by = "production_type") %>%
  mutate(pct = n / n_group * 100)

serotypes_to_show <- serotype_share %>%
  filter(pct >= 2) %>%
  distinct(Serotype) %>%
  pull(Serotype)

fig4_data <- serotype_share %>%
  mutate(Serotype = if_else(Serotype %in% serotypes_to_show, Serotype, "Other")) %>%
  group_by(production_type, Serotype) %>%
  summarise(pct = sum(pct), n = sum(n), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(Serotype = fct_reorder(Serotype, pct, .fun = max)) %>%
  mutate(Serotype = fct_relevel(Serotype, "Other", after = 0))

fig4 <- fig4_data %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = pct, y = Serotype, fill = production_type)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge2(preserve = "single"), color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = palette_qual[1:2]) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_percent(scale = 1)) +
  labs(
    title = "Serotype composition, by production type",
    subtitle = "% of isolates within each production type (controls for the 650 vs. 234 isolate group-size difference); serotypes <2% in both groups pooled as \"Other\"",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "Production type"
  ) +
  theme_apec() +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())

fig4
save_apec_plot(fig4, "fig4_serotype_share_by_production.png", stage = "drafts")
```

## Figure 5 (proposal_2): Variable virulence gene prevalence

The 6 core genes (hlyF, iroN, iss, iucC, iutA, ompT) are excluded - they are
near-ubiquitous in this dataset and would dominate/flatten the chart without
adding information. This is a magnitude comparison across many categories
(gene), so it gets a sequential single-hue ramp (not categorical) and is
capped to genes present in >=5% of isolates - rarer genes go to the
supplementary table rather than a 60+ row bar chart.

```{r figure5}
gene_prevalence <- virulence_long_variable %>%
  distinct(Sample, production_type, VF_gene_name) %>%
  count(VF_gene_name, name = "n_isolates") %>%
  mutate(pct = n_isolates / n_distinct(isolates$Sample) * 100) %>%
  arrange(desc(pct))

dir.create(here::here("results", "tables"), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
write_csv(gene_prevalence, here::here("results", "tables", "variable_virulence_gene_prevalence.csv"))

gene_prevalence_threshold <- 5  # % of isolates

fig5_data <- gene_prevalence %>%
  filter(pct >= gene_prevalence_threshold) %>%
  mutate(VF_gene_name = fct_reorder(VF_gene_name, pct))

fig5 <- fig5_data %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = pct, y = VF_gene_name, fill = pct)) +
  geom_col(color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#f7f7f7", high = palette_qual[1], guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_percent(scale = 1)) +
  labs(
    title = "Prevalence of variable virulence genes",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Core genes (hlyF, iroN, iss, iucC, iutA, ompT) excluded; genes present in <",
      gene_prevalence_threshold, "% of isolates omitted (see results/tables/variable_virulence_gene_prevalence.csv)"
    ),
    x = "% of isolates (n = 884)", y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_apec()

fig5
save_apec_plot(fig5, "fig5_variable_virulence_prevalence.png", stage = "drafts", height = 20)
```

**Proposal: split by production type**, since the underlying question is
usually "does virulence gene carriage differ between broiler and parent
flocks" rather than the pooled prevalence alone.

```{r figure5b}
gene_prevalence_by_type <- virulence_long_variable %>%
  distinct(Sample, production_type, VF_gene_name) %>%
  count(production_type, VF_gene_name, name = "n_isolates") %>%
  left_join(serotype_totals, by = "production_type") %>%
  mutate(pct = n_isolates / n_group * 100)

genes_to_show <- gene_prevalence %>% filter(pct >= gene_prevalence_threshold) %>% pull(VF_gene_name)

fig5b_data <- gene_prevalence_by_type %>%
  filter(VF_gene_name %in% genes_to_show) %>%
  mutate(VF_gene_name = factor(VF_gene_name, levels = levels(fig5_data$VF_gene_name)))

fig5b <- fig5b_data %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = pct, y = VF_gene_name, fill = production_type)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge2(preserve = "single"), color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = palette_qual[1:2]) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_percent(scale = 1)) +
  labs(
    title = "Prevalence of variable virulence genes, by production type",
    subtitle = "% within each production type (650 broiler, 234 parent flock isolates)",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "Production type"
  ) +
  theme_apec()

fig5b
save_apec_plot(fig5b, "fig5b_variable_virulence_by_production.png", stage = "drafts", height = 20)
```

## Figure 6: Top 10 ST x Serotype combinations, per year, isolates + sent cases in one graph

Different design goal from Figures 2/3/3b-e: instead of splitting "isolates
per combo," "combo by year," and "insendelser per year" into separate
figures, put isolate counts, production type and sent-case ("insendelse")
counts on one graph per year, and stack the years as rows so they're directly
comparable.

- **x-axis**: the same 10 ST : Serotype combinations in every panel (the
  overall top 10 by isolate count) - not the >=10-isolate set used in Figures
  2/3, which was 17 combinations.
- **Bar height** = isolate count, **stacked by production type** (Broiler /
  Parent flock) so that split stays visible.
- **Text above each bar** = number of sent cases (insendelser) for that
  combination that year, labeled in English as requested.
- **Facets = one column, one row per year, fixed x and y scales** (not
  `free_y`) so bar heights are directly comparable across years - a
  combination's bar in 2021 and its bar in 2019 are on the same scale.

```{r figure6 data}
top10_combos <- isolates %>%
  mutate(combo = paste(ST, Serotype, sep = " : ")) %>%
  count(combo, name = "n_total") %>%
  slice_max(n_total, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_total))

combo_levels_top10 <- top10_combos$combo

fig6_isolates <- isolates %>%
  mutate(combo = paste(ST, Serotype, sep = " : ")) %>%
  filter(combo %in% combo_levels_top10) %>%
  count(Year, combo, production_type, name = "n_isolates") %>%
  complete(Year, combo = combo_levels_top10, production_type, fill = list(n_isolates = 0)) %>%
  mutate(combo = factor(combo, levels = combo_levels_top10))

fig6_sent_cases <- isolates %>%
  mutate(combo = paste(ST, Serotype, sep = " : ")) %>%
  filter(combo %in% combo_levels_top10) %>%
  distinct(Year, combo, sak) %>%
  count(Year, combo, name = "n_sent_cases") %>%
  complete(Year, combo = combo_levels_top10, fill = list(n_sent_cases = 0))

fig6_bar_totals <- fig6_isolates %>%
  group_by(Year, combo) %>%
  summarise(n_isolates_total = sum(n_isolates), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(fig6_sent_cases, by = c("Year", "combo")) %>%
  mutate(combo = factor(combo, levels = combo_levels_top10))
```

```{r figure6}
fig6 <- fig6_isolates %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = combo, y = n_isolates, fill = production_type)) +
  geom_col(color = "white", linewidth = 0.15) +
  geom_text(
    data = fig6_bar_totals,
    aes(x = combo, y = n_isolates_total, label = paste0(n_sent_cases, " sent cases")),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, vjust = -0.4, size = 2.2, color = "grey20"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~Year, ncol = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = palette_qual[1:2]) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.2))) +
  labs(
    title = "Top 10 ST × Serotype combinations, by year",
    subtitle = "Bars = isolate count, stacked by production type; label = number of sent cases (insendelser) that year",
    x = "ST : Serotype", y = "Number of isolates", fill = "Production type"
  ) +
  theme_apec() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 7),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()
  )

fig6
save_apec_plot(fig6, "fig6_top10_st_serotype_by_year.png", stage = "drafts", width = 22, height = 42)
```

## Figure 6b: same as Figure 6, one year per page

Same data, same fixed y-axis (computed globally so every page is comparable),
one page/PNG per year for a closer look, following the same
`facet_wrap_paginate` approach as Figure 3d.

```{r figure6b}
y_max_fig6 <- fig6_bar_totals %>%
  mutate(y_top = n_isolates_total * 1.2) %>%
  pull(y_top) %>%
  max()

# NOTE: geom_text() below is given its own `data =` (it must be, since labels
# live at the bar-total level, not the per-production_type level of the main
# aes()). That means `<plot> + filter(...)` does NOT filter this layer - it
# only swaps the ggplot object's *default* data, and a layer with explicit
# `data` ignores the default entirely. So each per-year page is built fresh
# from year-filtered data for both layers, rather than reusing one base plot.
make_fig6b_plot <- function(yr) {
  fig6_isolates %>%
    filter(Year == yr) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = combo, y = n_isolates, fill = production_type)) +
    geom_col(color = "white", linewidth = 0.15) +
    geom_text(
      data = fig6_bar_totals %>% filter(Year == yr),
      aes(x = combo, y = n_isolates_total, label = paste0(n_sent_cases, " sent cases")),
      inherit.aes = FALSE, vjust = -0.4, size = 2.6, color = "grey20"
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = palette_qual[1:2]) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, y_max_fig6), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))) +
    labs(
      title = "Top 10 ST × Serotype combinations",
      subtitle = paste0("Year ", yr),
      x = "ST : Serotype", y = "Number of isolates", fill = "Production type"
    ) +
    theme_apec() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 8),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()
    )
}

by_year_dir_fig6 <- here::here("results", "figures", "drafts", "fig6b_by_year")
dir.create(by_year_dir_fig6, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

for (yr in sort(unique(fig6_isolates$Year))) {
  ggsave(
    filename = file.path(by_year_dir_fig6, paste0("fig6b_", yr, ".png")),
    plot = make_fig6b_plot(yr), width = 20, height = 14, units = "cm", dpi = 300
  )
}

pdf_path_fig6 <- here::here("results", "figures", "drafts", "fig6b_top10_st_serotype_by_year_pages.pdf")
pdf(pdf_path_fig6, width = 9, height = 6.5, onefile = TRUE)
for (yr in sort(unique(fig6_isolates$Year))) {
  print(make_fig6b_plot(yr))
}
invisible(dev.off())
```

## Figure 6c: Figure 6 with a mixed y-axis (shared scale + a highlighted outlier scale)

Figure 6's single fixed y-axis (0-227, driven by 2021's ST23:O78:H4 = 189
isolates) makes every other year's bars nearly invisible. Plain `free_y`
facets would fix readability but silently make every panel a different scale
- exactly the kind of chart that gets misread. The compromise: **one shared
y-axis for every year except the outlier**, and the outlier year keeps its
own taller axis but is visually marked (orange border/background + an
explicit "different y-axis scale" note) so nobody compares bar heights
across that boundary by eye. The outlier year is detected from the data
(largest single-bar total vs. the second-largest), not hardcoded to 2021, so
this keeps working if the underlying data changes.

`facet_wrap()` can't express "shared scale for most panels, separate scale
for one panel," so this stacks one ggplot per year with `patchwork` (new
dependency, added to renv.lock) instead - which also means x-axis labels
only need to be drawn once, on the bottom panel, since every panel shares the
same 10 combinations on the x-axis.

```{r figure6c}
library(patchwork)

panel_max_by_year <- fig6_bar_totals %>%
  group_by(Year) %>%
  summarise(panel_max = max(n_isolates_total), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(panel_max))

outlier_year <- panel_max_by_year$Year[1]
common_y_cap <- panel_max_by_year$panel_max[2] * 1.15
outlier_y_cap <- panel_max_by_year$panel_max[1] * 1.15

make_fig6c_panel <- function(yr, show_x_labels = FALSE) {
  is_outlier <- yr == outlier_year
  y_cap <- if (is_outlier) outlier_y_cap else common_y_cap

  p <- fig6_isolates %>%
    filter(Year == yr) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = combo, y = n_isolates, fill = production_type)) +
    geom_col(color = "white", linewidth = 0.15) +
    geom_text(
      data = fig6_bar_totals %>% filter(Year == yr),
      aes(x = combo, y = n_isolates_total, label = paste0(n_isolates_total, " (", n_sent_cases, " sent cases)")),
      inherit.aes = FALSE, vjust = -0.4, size = 2.3, color = "grey20"
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = palette_qual[1:2]) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, y_cap), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.06))) +
    labs(
      x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "Production type",
      subtitle = if (is_outlier) {
        paste0(yr, "  ⚠ different y-axis scale (0-", round(y_cap), " vs. 0-", round(common_y_cap), " for all other years)")
      } else {
        as.character(yr)
      }
    ) +
    theme_apec() +
    theme(
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(
        size = 9,
        face = if (is_outlier) "bold" else "plain",
        color = if (is_outlier) "#B45309" else "grey30"
      ),
      axis.text.x = if (show_x_labels) element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 8) else element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.x = if (show_x_labels) element_line(color = "grey60") else element_blank()
    )

  if (is_outlier) {
    p <- p + theme(
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#FFF3E0", color = "#B45309", linewidth = 0.9),
      plot.background = element_rect(color = "#B45309", linewidth = 0.9)
    )
  }
  p
}

years_sorted_fig6 <- sort(unique(fig6_isolates$Year))
fig6c_panels <- purrr::map(
  years_sorted_fig6,
  ~ make_fig6c_panel(.x, show_x_labels = (.x == max(years_sorted_fig6)))
)

fig6c <- wrap_plots(fig6c_panels, ncol = 1) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Top 10 ST × Serotype combinations, by year",
    subtitle = "Bars = isolate count, stacked by production type; label = total isolates (sent cases). Shared y-axis across years, EXCEPT the highlighted outlier year, which is not comparable to the others by bar height.",
    theme = theme_apec()
  ) &
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

fig6c
save_apec_plot(fig6c, "fig6c_top10_st_serotype_mixed_scale.png", stage = "drafts", width = 22, height = 40)
```

## Figure 8: ST x Serotype flow, by year (Year as an alluvial axis)

**Rejected (2026-07-30): kept for the record, not proposed to collaborators.**
Year has 8 categories, each connecting to 8-13 different STs - a dense
many-to-many bipartite graph. The barycenter ordering that cleaned up
Figures 3e/3b (which only had to sort against 2 production-type categories)
cannot untangle this; it is close to a worst case for crossing minimization,
not a rendering bug to fix. Figure 8b (faceting by production type instead
of coloring by it) does not fix the underlying tangle either, and
additionally compresses the smaller Parent flock facet under a shared
y-axis. If this is ever revisited, it would need a much smaller x-axis (e.g.
top 3-4 STs only) to have any chance of reading cleanly - noted here so we
don't have to rediscover that by rebuilding it.

```{r figure8 data}
alluvial_year_data <- isolates %>%
  mutate(combo = paste(ST, Serotype, sep = " : ")) %>%
  filter(combo %in% top_combos$combo) %>%
  count(Year, ST, Serotype, production_type, name = "n")

year_order <- as.character(sort(unique(alluvial_year_data$Year)))

st_order_yr <- alluvial_year_data %>%
  mutate(year_pos = match(as.character(Year), year_order)) %>%
  group_by(ST) %>%
  summarise(bary = weighted.mean(year_pos, w = n), n_total = sum(n), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(bary, desc(n_total)) %>%
  pull(ST) %>%
  as.character()

serotype_order_yr <- alluvial_year_data %>%
  mutate(st_pos = match(as.character(ST), st_order_yr)) %>%
  group_by(Serotype) %>%
  summarise(bary = weighted.mean(st_pos, w = n), n_total = sum(n), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(bary, desc(n_total)) %>%
  pull(Serotype) %>%
  as.character()

alluvial_year_data <- alluvial_year_data %>%
  mutate(
    Year_f = factor(as.character(Year), levels = year_order),
    ST = factor(ST, levels = st_order_yr),
    Serotype = factor(Serotype, levels = serotype_order_yr)
  )
```

```{r figure8}
fig8 <- alluvial_year_data %>%
  ggplot(aes(axis1 = Year_f, axis2 = ST, axis3 = Serotype, y = n)) +
  geom_alluvium(aes(fill = production_type), width = 1/5, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_stratum(width = 1/5, fill = "grey95", color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_text(stat = "stratum", aes(label = after_stat(stratum)), size = 2.0) +
  scale_x_discrete(limits = c("Year", "ST", "Serotype"), expand = c(0.08, 0.08)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = palette_qual[1:2]) +
  labs(
    title = "ST × Serotype flow, by year",
    subtitle = paste0("Combinations with ≥", combo_threshold, " isolates total; color = production type; axes ordered to reduce crossing"),
    x = NULL, y = "Isolates", fill = "Production type"
  ) +
  theme_apec() +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom")

fig8
save_apec_plot(fig8, "fig8_year_st_serotype_alluvial.png", stage = "drafts", width = 30, height = 22)
```

## Figure 8b: same axes as Figure 8, faceted by production type instead of colored

**Rejected (2026-07-30), same reasons as Figure 8** - the Year → ST tangle
persists within each facet, and the shared y-axis compresses the Parent
flock panel.

```{r figure8b}
alluvial_facet_data <- isolates %>%

fig8b <- alluvial_facet_data %>%

  labs(
    title = "ST × Serotype flow, by year, faceted by production type",
    subtitle = paste0("Combinations with ≥", combo_threshold, " isolates total; same axis order as Figure 8"),
    x = NULL, y = "Isolates", fill = "Production type"
  ) +
  theme_apec() +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_blank(), legend.position = "none")

fig8b
save_apec_plot(fig8b, "fig8b_year_st_serotype_alluvial_facet_production.png", stage = "drafts", width = 30, height = 30)
```
